newsitem.title: USA: Pa. airport divestiture group calls for new agency.
newsitem.headline: Pa. airport divestiture group calls for new agency.

text.p: Pennsylvania State Transportation Secretary Bradley L Mallory announced Thursday that an advisory group of local citizens has recommended the creation of a regional aviation authority to pursue the acquisition and operation of the state-owned Harrisburg International and Capital City airports.

"These two airports contribute greatly to the economic vitality and quality of life in southcentral Pennsylvania," Mallory said in a statement. "It makes sense that they be run by an authority accountable to the people, businesses and industries that take advantage of the services provided by the airports."

Discussions about a local takeover of the airports began in last July with the creation of the Airport Divestiture Group (ADG), an advisory group of citizens from the counties of Cumberland, Dauphin and York and the cities of Harrisburg and York.
The ADG is recommending that each participating municipality consider passage of a resolution authorizing its participation in the Susquehanna Area Regional Aviation Authority (SARAA).
Membership would consist of three appointees from each county and two appointees from each city for a total of 13.

Suggested articles of incorporation would authorize the authority to "engage in acquiring, holding, constructing, financing, improving, maintaining, operating, owning and leasing all assets" of Harrisburg International Airport and the Capital City Airport, York County.
